contexts.text: There was heard from them a sound of murmurs pretty tumultuous...
The first temptation is described by the murmuring of the sons of Israel when they saw the army of Pharaoh.
It treats of the second temptation of those of the Spiritual Church, which is described by the murmuring of the people at Marah.
The people murmured against Moses () = a feeling of grief (or pain) from the bitterness of the temptation. To murmur = complaint, such as there is in temptations.

The temptations which those of the Lord's Spiritual Church underwent after they had been delivered from infestations; and also the temptations which those who are of that Church will undergo, are described by the murmurings of the sons of Israel in the wilderness; and, as spiritual temptations are commonly carried on to despair, by to murmur is signified complaint from the feeling of grief in the temptations. Illustrated.
All the company of the sons of Israel murmured () = a feeling of grief, and complaint on account of the weight of the temptation.
In His hearing your murmurings () = that their complaints would cease... Murmurings = a feeling of grief from the bitterness of the temptation, and the consequent complaints. AC 8433.
And what are we, that ye murmur against us? () = that the complaints were against the Divine... To murmur = complaint. AC 8434.
Because He hath heard your murmurings () = that He will bring aid on account of the feeling of grief in the temptation.
I have heard the murmurings of the sons of Israel () = that the complaints which are from the temptation will cease.
This (fourth) temptation is signified by the murmuring of the sons of Israel because they had no water.
The people murmured against Moses () = a greater degree of the feeling of grief.
I heard a hostile murmur from the Lower Regions...
I once heard an unwonted murmur from afar, and followed the direction of the sound...
The tumult of such murmurs, or the sound of confused murmurs, was of a threefold kind. Described.
When Sirens arrive, they continually murmur something...
They drove them away by concentrating their murmurs, and thus their forces, into them.

The murmuring (of Korah, etc.), against Moses and Aaron, signified the profanation of the good of celestial love... For to murmur, that is, to rebel against the Lord, and to perform holy things, is profanation.
